{{one source|date=April 2025}}
In mathematics, especially [[algebraic topology]], a '''simplicial diagram''' is a diagram indexed by the [[simplex category]] (= the category consisting of all <math>[n] = \{ 0, 1, \cdots n \}</math> and the order-preserving functions).

Formally, a simplicial diagram in a category or an ∞-category ''C'' is a contraviant functor from the simplex category to ''C''. Thus, it is the same thing as a [[simplicial object]] but is typically thought of as a sequence of objects in ''C'' that is depicted using multiple arrows
:<math>\cdots \, \underset{\rightrightarrows}\rightrightarrows \, U_2 \, \underset{\rightarrow}\rightrightarrows \, U_1 \, \rightrightarrows\, U_0</math>
where <math>U_n</math> is the image of <math>[n]</math> from <math>\Delta</math> in ''C''.

A typical example is the [[Čech nerve]] of a map <math>U \to X</math>; i.e., <math>U_0 = U, U_1 = U \times_X U, \dots</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Khan|2023|loc=Definition 2.1.6.}}</ref> If ''F'' is a presheaf with values in an ∞-category and <math>U_{\bullet}</math> a Čech nerve, then <math>F(U_{\bullet})</math> is a cosimplicial diagram and saying <math>F</math> is a sheaf exactly means that <math>F(X)</math> is the limit of <math>F(U_{\bullet})</math> for each <math>U \to X</math> in a [[Grothendieck topology]]. See also: [[simplicial presheaf]].

If <math>U_{\bullet}</math> is a simplicial diagram, then the colimit
:<math>[U_{\bullet}] := \varinjlim_{[n] \in \Delta} U_n</math>
is called the '''geometric realization''' of <math>U_{\bullet}</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Khan|2023|loc=Notation 4.1.6.}}</ref> For example, if <math>U_n = X \times G^n</math> is an [[action groupoid]], then the geometric realization in '''Grpd''' is the [[quotient groupoid]] <math>[X/G]</math> which contains more information than the set-theoretic quotient <math>X/G</math>.<ref>{{harvnb|Khan|2023|loc=Ch. 4, before § 4.1.}}</ref> A [[quotient stack]] is an instance of this construction (perhaps up to [[stackification]]).

The limit of a cosimplicial diagram is called the '''totalization''' of it.<ref>{{harvnb|Khan|2023|loc=Definition 3.2.3.}}</ref>

== Augmented simplicial diagram ==
Sometimes one uses an augmented version of a simplicial diagram. Formally, an augmented simplicial diagram  is a contravariant functor from the [[augmented simplex category]] <math>\Delta_{\textrm{aug}}</math> where the objects are <math>[n] = \{ 0, 1, \dots, n \}, \, n \ge -1</math> and the morphisms order-preserving functions.
